content:
HubSpot Company Record — Redwood Inference

Account snapshot
- Company: KumoCart (kumocart.com)
- Segment: Mid-market, APAC-heavy traffic profile (SEA + ANZ + India; small NA footprint)
- Current stage: Evaluation (post-demo; comparing vendors; wants proof on region coverage + economics)
- Owner: Stephanie Nguyen (AE)
- SE: Markus Klein

What they’re building / why now
- Consumer marketplace app with: (1) in-app support agent, (2) order issue summarization for human agents, (3) product search + reranking.
- “APAC is where we feel latency pain the most; we can’t keep routing everything to US.”
- They got budget approved for 2025 to consolidate LLM inference (currently a mix of vendor API + some self-hosted GPU in SG).

Workloads + technical requirements
- Workloads:
  - Chat-style generation for support agent + internal agent assist (streaming required)
  - Embeddings for product catalog + ticket search (batch + online)
  - Reranking for search results (latency-sensitive)
- Latency targets (stated on call; not fully validated):
  - Chat first-token: wants “snappy in APAC” (goal < 250–350ms TTFT in-region for typical prompts)
  - End-to-end p95 for short answers: target < 2.5–3.0s (depends on output length)
  - Reranking: p95 < 150ms for top-k requests at moderate QPS
- Throughput:
  - Peak bursts during campaigns; needs predictable behavior during spikes
  - Wants clear quota/limits story + ability to reserve/burst
- Cost sensitivity:
  - Finance cares about unit cost per resolved ticket + per search session
  - Explicit interest in “latency/$” framing (they want both speed and cost, not cost-only)

Model preferences / constraints
- Open models preferred for cost + control; will accept Redwood-curated catalog.
- They asked specifically: “If we pin a model version, can you guarantee same behavior across regions?”
  - Answer given: model version pinning supported; perf can vary by region/hardware; publish per-region tables; recommend canary + fallback policies.
- Interested in fallback behaviors:
  - If APAC region is constrained, they want predictable fallback to another APAC region first (avoid jumping to US by default)
  - Need to understand how Redwood routing policies interact with data residency constraints

Region coverage questions (core theme)
- They are APAC-heavy and repeatedly asked for:
  - Exact APAC regions available today (and which are roadmap)
  - Whether APAC regions are included in the public benchmark report tables and how to interpret them
  - Guidance on region selection headers / API configuration to force region vs allow multi-region routing
- Internal note: This account is very likely to engage with the benchmark report content; include APAC region table screenshots + methodology disclaimers; avoid absolute “fastest” claims.

Security / compliance
- Not a regulated industry, but security team requires:
  - SOC 2 report availability
  - Audit logging for admin actions + request metadata
  - KMS (cloud KMS ok)
  - Retention controls (don’t store prompts longer than necessary; configurable)
  - Data residency expectations: keep APAC user data in APAC where feasible; document any cross-region failover behavior
- They did NOT ask for air-gapped/on-prem.

Competitive context
- Evaluating: Together AI, AWS Bedrock, and self-hosted vLLM as baseline.
- Their POV: Bedrock easy procurement but perf/cost uncertain; self-hosting is “ops tax”; they want a platform that can show hard numbers by region.

Recent activity timeline (most recent first)
- 2025-03-11 — Email from Markus (SE) answering routing/fallback + region pinning questions; proposed 45-min deep dive w/ diagrams. Pending.
- 2025-03-06 — Internal: flagged to Marketing/Growth that this account should get the APAC-specific benchmark follow-up sequence (model/region spotlight).
- 2025-03-03 — Demo completed (Hosted API + basic observability walkthrough). They liked cost/latency breakdown view.
- 2025-02-24 — Discovery call: main concern is APAC latency; asked for “benchmark proof” + reproduction steps.
- 2025-02-12 — Inbound via benchmark landing page waitlist form (UTM indicates APAC region interest). SDR noted: “asked if you have Singapore/Tokyo; wants chart/table by region.”

Notes (call snippets / verbatims)
- “We can’t sell ‘AI support’ if Manila and Sydney see 2–3s just to start responding.”
- “We need a plan for when a region is having a bad day—fallback needs to be deterministic and not violate our data residency commitments.”
- “If you publish latency/$ by region, we’ll take that to procurement. We just need to understand the caveats.”

Next steps (proposed)
1) Share APAC rows from the benchmark region tables (sanitized public subset when available) + short explanation of how to read latency/$.
2) Schedule technical deep dive (Stephanie + Markus + their platform lead):
   - Region selection: how to pin region vs allow multi-region
   - Fallback order recommendations for APAC-heavy apps
   - How to test with their prompt/sequence distribution (small reproduction harness)
3) If APAC coverage meets requirements: start 2-week POC (chat + embeddings + reranking) with success criteria:
   - p95 targets in two APAC regions
   - cost per 1M tokens within agreed range
   - documented runbook for failover and incident behavior

Internal reminders
- When sending benchmark materials: include variance language + methodology appendix; do NOT claim universal superiority.
- Emphasize that regional results differ; point them to per-region tables and routing guidance.
- Offer Dedicated as optional path if they need tighter throughput/latency predictability during campaign peaks.
